identity.name: load_heritage
identity.description: Loads Toronto's Heritage Register (Part IV / Part V points) into heritage_properties and the Heritage Conservation Districts (polygons) into heritage_districts from two CKAN zipped shapefiles. Each dataset is gated, acquired, validated and written on its own (DEC-K): a guarded upsert on source_id plus an F-C1-guarded departure delete, one transaction per dataset.

why_lock.text: Mutual exclusion with every other writer of heritage_properties / heritage_districts (Spec 47 §A.5 row 61, DEC-A: lock = spec number); the shell keeps `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 61;` as a §5.4 source-text constant, asserted equal by the pipeline advisory-lock suite.

why.text: Legacy `INSERT INTO heritage_properties ... ON CONFLICT (source_id) DO UPDATE SET` (all 11 step columns + updated_at) guarded by `WHERE heritage_properties.geom/status/designated_date/address_text/source_dataset_version IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.*` [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:405-417], then `DELETE FROM heritage_properties WHERE source_id <> ALL($1::BIGINT[])` behind the F-C1 empty-set guard [READ :594-606], both in ONE transaction for this dataset. The guard set is the legacy one byte for byte, version stamp included (LH-D2 PIN, ④c).

Legacy `INSERT INTO heritage_districts ... ON CONFLICT (source_id) DO UPDATE SET` guarded by `WHERE heritage_districts.geom/name/designated_date/source_dataset_version IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.*` [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:441-451], then the F-C1-guarded departure DELETE [READ :594-606], one transaction for this dataset. Guard set = legacy (LH-D2 PIN).
Per dataset: the batched guarded upsert and the departure DELETE, each dataset in its own transaction (2 targets x 2 statements). The batched geometry validation is a pure SELECT and writes nothing.

on_prior_run_error_why.text: LH-D3 PIN (parity). The legacy `readPriorRunMeta(...).catch(...)` logged `prior-run query failed (treating as no baseline)` and loaded both datasets as a first run [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:684-689]. warn_row keeps that behaviour and adds the library WARN row, so it is no longer silent; ④a moves it to fail_step (LR-D2 precedent).

why.text: Migration 227 enables RLS class-B default-deny on heritage_properties with 0 policies [READ migrations/227_rls_class_b_default_deny.sql:53]: the upsert and DELETE work only under rolbypassrls, else they affect 0 rows while the verdict reads PASS.
Same as heritage_properties [READ migrations/227_rls_class_b_default_deny.sql:52].
The point GIST index enrich_heritage joins parcels through (§11.1); without it the consumer degrades to a sequential scan.
The geography GIST index enrich_heritage's distance match uses (enrich-heritage.descriptor.json declares the same pair).
The polygon GIST index the district containment join uses.

batch_why.text: MQ-B1 (a), registry-truth fold 19: two write targets, and the ingest writer strides EACH by pipeline.maxRowsPerInsert(columnsPerRow) (scripts/lib/step/write.js executeWrite): heritage_properties 12 columns -> 5461 rows, heritage_districts 9 -> 7281. One number cannot state both, so batch is "none" (generated by scripts/generate-ingest-batch.js); no ingest runner reads execution.batch.

on_row_error_why.text: A feature that fails geometry validation is counted and the dataset continues [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:565-577]; the tolerance is bounded by the FAIL-severity, config-resolved pre_write check heritage_geometry_skipped_pct.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value the library already measured, so a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition — it must redden the run rather than drop its row.

why.text: The legacy INFO row `push('dataset_source_license', LICENSE_URL, 'INFO')` [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:675]. Both externals declare the same Toronto Open Data licence, so the row reports it once; a primary with no licence reads 1.

Legacy WARN row pushed only when HERITAGE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT=1 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:677-679]; now always present, WARN exactly when the override stands, so a run that proceeded past L7 says so on its own record.
Legacy WARN row pushed only when HERITAGE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE=1 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:678-680]; now always present, WARN exactly when the override stands.

Legacy WARN row pushed only when HERITAGE_FORCE_RELOAD=1 (the additive force seam, 451962ac, operator ruling 2026-10-01, pushed right after the mass-delete override row); now always present, WARN exactly when override.force_run stands, so a forced reload says so on its own record and the forced PRE and POST captures carry the same row.

expect.reports: the heritage_register gate decision that skipped it, or null when it loaded

why.text: Legacy INFO row `heritage_register_load_skipped` with the skip reason, pushed only on a skip [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:744]. DEC-K: each dataset is gated on its own; detail null means the register was acquired.

expect.reports: the heritage_districts gate decision that skipped it, or null when it loaded

why.text: Legacy INFO row `heritage_districts_load_skipped` [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:745]; DEC-K per-dataset skip, detail null when acquired.

L9 staleness: WARN when the older dataset's Last-Modified is more than the configured number of Julian years old [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:180-183, :725-726]. value = age in Julian years (fractional, the exact legacy comparison ageDays > years x 365.25); detail = the legacy whole-year floor. An unparseable/absent Last-Modified reports inert (INFO), exactly as the legacy datasetAgeStatus(null) did.

expect.violation_when: a dataset with no prior sub-block acquires zero features

order_guarantee.guarantee: A zero-feature first run must FAIL before any write — the dataset is refused, the other dataset still loads (DEC-K).

why.text: L14 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:538-546]: a first run that parses zero features is a corrupt or empty source, not an empty load. A LATER zero-feature run is not this check: it proceeds and the F-C1 empty-set guard suppresses the departure DELETE (L15).

expect.vs: the dataset's prior completed sub-block feature_count (worst of the two datasets)

order_guarantee.guarantee: A feature-count drift beyond the bound must stop that dataset before its transaction opens; the override enables the write but never removes the FAIL row.

why.text: L7 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:548-558, :712-714]: |loaded - prior| / prior above the bound FAILs and the dataset is not written. HERITAGE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT=1 lets the write proceed and never suppresses the FAIL row (override.accept_anomaly).

expect.of: features dropped by the geometry validation over the dataset's feature count (worst of the two datasets)

order_guarantee.guarantee: More than the bound of features failing geometry validation must abort the dataset before its transaction opens.

why.text: L8 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:578-586, :708-710]: more than the bound of a dataset's features failing validation aborts that dataset before its transaction; no override exists for L8.

expect.reports: the heritage_register sub-block feature_count (a skipped register carries the prior count)

why.text: Legacy INFO row [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:701]: the register sub-block feature_count, i.e. the deduped kept count on a load, the prior count on a skip, 0 on a failed acquisition (LH-D8).
Legacy INFO row [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:702]; same semantics as the register row.

why.text: Legacy INFO row [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:704-706]: the L25 Listed filter share of the raw register. Purely descriptive.

why.text: Legacy WARN when > 0 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:729]: an unknown STATUS value is L25 vocabulary drift upstream (DEC-I).

why.text: Legacy WARN when > 0 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:730]: HCD vocabulary drift (DEC-I).

why.text: Legacy WARN when > 0 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:733] (DEC-M: address_text is NOT NULL, so a missing ADDRESS is stored as '' and counted, via the shapeRecord tag address_coerced_empty).

why.text: Legacy WARN when > 0 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:736]: the #426 key-rename canary (OBJECTID -> Folder_Row, 78748a36) — a renamed key must be loud, never a silent zero-row PASS.

expect.reports: district features whose HCD_NO does not coerce to a positive integer

why.text: Legacy WARN when > 0 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:737].
Legacy WARN when > 0 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:738]: dedupeBySourceId keeps the first feature per Folder_Row (ON CONFLICT cannot affect a row twice).
Legacy WARN when > 0 [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:739].

expect.of: departed rows over the dataset's prior feature_count (worst of the two datasets)

why.text: L7c [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:607-613, :716-718]. LH-D1 PIN: scored AFTER the dataset's transaction committed, exactly as the legacy did; ④c moves it before the write. HERITAGE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE=1 lets the run complete and never suppresses the FAIL row.

expect.vs: updated rows over the dataset's prior feature_count (worst of the two datasets)

why.text: L7b [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:607, :720-722]. LH-D2 PIN: source_dataset_version sits inside the IS DISTINCT FROM guard, so a new CKAN version rewrites every row and this reads ~1 WARN on a version-only change (run 1277: 28/28 HCDs, pct 1.0).

expect.violation_when: the register was not written: acquisition threw, or a pre_write check refused it

why.text: Legacy FAIL row `heritage_register_load_failed` with the fail reason [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:742]. DEC-K: the other dataset still loads (on_failure fail_row_continue). detail = the error or the refusing checks; null when the register loaded or skipped.

expect.violation_when: the districts were not written: acquisition threw, or a pre_write check refused them

why.text: Legacy FAIL row `heritage_districts_load_failed` [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:743]; same semantics as the register row.

The legacy env read `process.env.HERITAGE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT === '1'` [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:470, :552]: when the city genuinely re-publishes a dataset at a different size an operator accepts the drift for ONE run; the FAIL row survives.

The legacy env read `process.env.HERITAGE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE === '1'` [READ scripts/load-heritage.js:471, :613]: the #426 re-key (78748a36) used it for the one-time full re-key; the run completes and the FAIL row stays.

deviations.from: LH-D8 (a) — a per-dataset failure returned `{ failed: true }`, which `pipeline.run` ignored, so a STANDALONE run exited 0 and its ledger row read `completed` with verdict FAIL (legacy :768; pipeline.js:589-600)

why.text: The library maps a FAIL verdict with an unaccepted FAIL row to status FAILED, so a standalone run whose dataset failed now reads `failed`. In the sources chain run-chain stamps the step row from the exit code and rolls the chain up as completed_with_errors, exactly as before (chain parity). 0x adds no status override. (b), the failed dataset's zero skeleton sub-block, is PINNED (compute buildLoadMeta) and fixed at ④b.

deviations.adjudicated_by: plan re-grounding row 24 / §3 HR-D8 split (0x RE-FREEZE #29), orchestrator ① decision 4

deviations.from: LH-D11 — tally order: the legacy classified STATUS / HCD_TYPE (L25) BEFORE coercing the key and checking the geometry (`const cls = classifyRegisterStatus(p.STATUS)` :328 before `coerceSourceId(p.Folder_Row)` :334)

why.text: The acquisition seam (acquire.js parseShapefile) coerces the key and drops a null geometry before compute.shapeRecord classifies, so a Listed / Under-Appeal feature with a bad key or no geometry now counts as bad-key / null-geometry instead of filtered. Exposure 0: 0 bad keys and 0 null geometries in 12,332 + 32 raw features [MEASURED 2026-09-30 ① §A.F-NET].

deviations.from: the audit row set — the legacy pushed the override / bad-id / duplicate / load_failed / load_skipped rows only when they fired, and scored non-INFO rows PASS as INFO (:675-745)

why.text: Every legacy row is a declared check that emits on every run (PASS / INFO at zero, the ravines LR precedent), so silence no longer means both "zero" and "not counted". A failed or refused dataset additionally lands the library row `primary_failed:<id>` (FAIL, errored, 0x on_failure fail_row_continue) beside the legacy-named heritage_<id>_load_failed row (① decision 2).

deviations.from: the gated-skip sub-block — legacy re-emitted `{ ...skeletonSub(), ...priorSub, spec_version, features_inserted: 0, features_updated: 0, features_deleted: 0, skipped_reason }` and its specSub rename reset filtered_out_* / unknown_*_count to 0 (:493, :526-530, :654-657)

why.text: A skipped dataset is re-emitted by the library (multiPrimarySkipEmit / buildSkipReEmitMeta: skeleton <- prior <- {spec_version, skipped_reason}), so features_* and the filtered / unknown counters CARRY the prior run's values instead of zeroes. The consumer reads spec_version, feature_count, drift_check_passed and source_dataset_version only [READ scripts/lib/compute/enrich-heritage.js:44-80], all identical.

deviations.adjudicated_by: orchestrator ② ruling (0x DS4 re-emit, ravines precedent)

deviations.from: heritage_<id>_load_failed on a post-commit mass delete — legacy set the dataset outcome `failed` when L7c breached without HERITAGE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE (:613), which pushed the load_failed row

why.text: The mass delete is reported by heritage_mass_delete_pct (FAIL, accept_anomaly-coverable); heritage_<id>_load_failed now means "not written" (acquisition threw or a pre_write check refused), so an accepted mass delete cannot leave an unaccepted FAIL row behind. Verdict unchanged (FAIL either way without the override).

deviations.from: the order of L7 and L8 — legacy aborted on count drift BEFORE running the validation SQL (:549-563), so a drift-failed dataset never reported a geometry skip

why.text: The library validates geometry before the pre_write gate and scores L14, L7 and L8 together, so a dataset breaching both reports both FAIL rows; the write is refused either way (no transaction opens). The drift-failed sub-block keeps the legacy shape (feature_count, drift_check_passed false).

deviations.from: `loadMarketplaceConfigs(pool, 'source-heritage')` + the Zod ConfigSchema literals (:51-58, :667-668), which also read trade_configurations

why.text: LH-D4 closed: the six knobs plus the round3 scale are declared config.logic_variables resolved by the library into ctx.config (seeded, defaults byte-equal to the Zod literals). The trade_configurations read had no heritage consumer and is retired.

deviations.from: the step's own SQL reads of pipeline_runs, logic_variables and trade_configurations (reads evidence table, assessment §11)

why.text: Intentionally NOT declared in inputs.reads.tables: the prior-run read (pipeline_runs records_meta by pipeline/status, ORDER BY started_at) is the library's staleness.readPriorEmitWithPosture, the logic_variables read is the library config resolver, the advisory lock / NOW() / ledger rows are the runner's, and trade_configurations is retired (deviation above). inputs.reads.tables is reserved for domain tables the step reads; its own write targets' guard and key reads are declared by outputs.writes[].write_discipline.guard_columns and key.

deviations.adjudicated_by: operator new-conversion rule 2026-09-30 (reads evidence table), explicit omission

deviations.from: the inline POINT_VALIDATION_SQL / POLYGON_VALIDATION_SQL (:65-112) and the per-dataset temp-dir download / unzip / locate / parse (:253-384)

why.text: Replaced by the library seams (acquire.js download + parseShapefile, write.js validateGeometries with geometry_kind point / polygon). Same accept / repair / collection-extract / skip classes; the one residue is LH-D9 (limitations).

PIPELINE_META is derived from the descriptor (external ids plus declared columns), so it cannot drift from what the step reads and writes; the externals are now named heritage_register / heritage_districts (① decision 1) and created_at is declared written:"db_default".

deviations.from: the legacy loader had no force switch until the additive HERITAGE_FORCE_RELOAD seam (451962ac, operator ruling 2026-10-01) — before it, a dataset reloaded only when CKAN moved

why.text: override.force_run HERITAGE_FORCE_RELOAD bypasses both staleness tiers for both datasets (the RAVINE_FORCE_RELOAD precedent); it changes what is acquired only, never how it is written. The legacy seam (451962ac) uses the SAME key, so the ① PRE and ② POST golden captures force identically; unset, both are byte-identical to normal runs.

deviations.adjudicated_by: plan §8 ② (ravines / centreline precedent) + operator ruling 2026-10-01 (legacy seam)

limitations.what: LH-D6 — a standalone run reads and writes the ledger name `load_heritage`, while enrich_heritage reads only `sources:load_heritage` [READ scripts/lib/compute/enrich-heritage.js:28], so a standalone load is invisible to the consumer (legacy hard-coded PIPELINE_NAME for the prior read only).
limitations.measured: 0 standalone load_heritage ledger rows on record [MEASURED 2026-09-30 ① §A.F-DB]

limitations.what: LH-D9 — the library point arm accepts a single-member MultiPoint (ST_NumGeometries(ST_CollectionExtract(repaired, 1)) = 1) that the legacy point validation skipped as skipped_unsupported_type.
limitations.measured: 0 non-Point register features (12,332 raw, all Point) [MEASURED 2026-09-30 ① §A.F-NET]

limitations.what: LH-D1 — the L7c mass-delete FAIL is scored after the dataset's transaction committed, and enrich_heritage checks drift_check_passed only, never mass_delete_check_passed; ④c moves it to pre_write over a dry-run departure count.
limitations.measured: 0 mass-delete breaches in 8 sources:load_heritage runs [MEASURED 2026-09-30 ① §A.F-DB]

limitations.what: LH-D2 — source_dataset_version is a guard column, so every new CKAN version rewrites every row and heritage_geometry_update_pct counts version-stamp rewrites; ④c narrows the guard.
limitations.measured: run 1277: 28/28 districts updated, geometry_update_pct 1.0 WARN [MEASURED ① §1.3]

limitations.what: LH-D10 — the source carries one register row with construction_year 1250 (source_id 2433372) and the loader has no plausibility bound; a post-conversion WARN is filed, not in scope.

recovery.reset: TRUNCATE is never correct here — re-run with HERITAGE_FORCE_RELOAD=1, which bypasses both staleness tiers for both datasets and rewrites through the same guarded upsert plus departure delete.

interrupted_why.text: Rule 12 truthful posture: both targets declare retract "departed" (a scoped departure DELETE that always fires inside the same per-dataset transaction as its upsert), not retract "all" / full_only, so force_full_on_next_run is not owed. A kill mid-run leaves each dataset either fully committed or rolled back; a re-run re-gates each dataset against its last completed sub-block.

before_image_why.text: The generic before-image mechanism (write.js writeBeforeImage) mirrors a retraction's write_discipline.scope as a SELECT; both targets declare scope "none" with retract "departed", so there is no scoped retraction to mirror, and every column is re-derived from the source on a forced reload.

why.text: Both datasets were gated and either loaded or skipped (DEC-K), and every check passed. A skipped dataset re-emits its prior sub-block (DS4), so the completed row always carries both sub-blocks for enrich_heritage.

A WARN check tripped with no FAIL: an unknown STATUS / HCD_TYPE, a coerced-empty address, a bad or duplicate key, a standing override, a stale dataset, or a version-stamp rewrite (LH-D2 geometry_update_pct).
A declared FAIL check tripped and its override.accept_anomaly env was standing (HERITAGE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT / HERITAGE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE): the run completes and the FAIL row stays.
L14: a dataset with no prior sub-block parsed zero features; that dataset is not written, the other still loads (DEC-K).
L7 tripped with no standing HERITAGE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT: the dataset was refused at pre_write (no transaction opened) and the other dataset still loads.
L8 tripped: more than the bound of a dataset's features failed geometry validation; that dataset was refused at pre_write.
L7c tripped with no standing HERITAGE_ACCEPT_MASS_DELETE — scored after the commit (LH-D1 PIN).

The register HEAD / download / parse threw (on_failure fail_row_continue): the FAIL row plus the library primary_failed:heritage_register row, the districts still load (DEC-K). Standalone status FAILED is the LH-D8 (a) deviation; the zero skeleton sub-block is LH-D8 (b).
Same as the register terminal, for the districts dataset.

A step-level throw outside a dataset's catch: the once-per-step write-privilege preflight (before any dataset is acquired), a row-conservation mismatch, or a transaction error. Nothing further is written.
Advisory lock 61 is held by another process. Legacy returned with no summary at all (the SDK SKIP carried no audit_table); the library now emits a row-derived SKIP summary.
